earlier_scan.source_named: Lienhard, Ruth & M. Giger. Daba phonological description (SIL Cameroon; cf. Lienhard & Giger 2009 cited on Glottolog); SIL page 403-blocked.

new_statements.quote: Dans la langue daba chaque syllabe est charactérisée par un ton propre. Trois régistres tonals sont observés : haut (marqué par un accent ́ ), moyen (non marqué dans les formes orthographiques, mais avec an accent ̄ dans les formes phonétiques) et bas (marqué par un accent ̀ ). En plus nous avons relevé un ton modulé bas (marqué par un accent ̂ ) sur certains pronoms sujet. [...] L'opposition entre les tons a très peu de distribution sur le plan lexical.
new_statements.translation: In the Daba language every syllable is characterised by its own tone. Three tonal registers are observed: high (marked with an acute accent), mid (unmarked in orthographic forms, but with a macron in phonetic forms) and low (marked with a grave accent). In addition we have noted a low modulated (falling) tone (marked with a circumflex) on certain subject pronouns. [...] The opposition between tones has very little distribution on the lexical level.
new_statements.citation: Lienhard, Ruth & M. Giger. 1986 (révisé en 2009). Document de référence pour la standardisation de la langue daba. Yaoundé: Société Internationale de Linguistique.
new_statements.locator: §2.5.1 'Les tonèmes' and §2.5.3 'Fonction du ton', printed pp. 14-15 (PDF pp. 15-16)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (28 pp., pdfinfo; text layer present). Title page: "Document de référence pour la standardisation de la langue daba, par R. Lienhard et M. Giger, Société Internationale de Linguistique, Yaoundé, 1986 (révisé en 2009)". The quoted passage is verbatim at §2.5.1 "Les tonèmes", printed p. 14 = PDF p. 15: "Dans la langue daba chaque syllabe est charactérisée par un ton propre. Trois régistres tonals sont observés : haut (marqué par un accent ́), moyen (non marqué dans les formes orthographiques, mais avec an accent ̄ dans les formes phonétiques) et bas (marqué par un accent ̀). En plus nous avons relevé un ton modulé bas (marqué par un accent ̂) sur certains pronoms sujet." and the second…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Daba is a register-tone language: every syllable bears one of three level tones (H, M, L), plus a low falling tone on some subject pronouns; tone melodies are restricted by word class (monosyllabic verbs only L or M; first tone of disyllabic verbs always L; first tone of di-/trisyllabic nouns L or M; adverbs, adjectives and ideophones often H-initial). Tone is marginally lexical but marks grammatical categories (subject focus, verb emphasis, perfective/imperfective, directional, clause relations). The source says nothing about word stress or accent d'intensité.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned (no stress discussed at all).
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. Tone-pattern restrictions by word class (verbs vs nouns vs adverbs/adjectives/ideophones); one unresolved case, the pronoun ta, whose meanings differ by tone and vowel length (§2.5.4).
new_statements.domain_note: Description is at the level of the phonological word (mots monosyllabiques/dissyllabiques/trisyllabiques) with phrase-level grammatical tone also described; based on the Pologozom variety used as the standard.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted source describes the Pologozom variety (Daba proper), which SIL used as the reference dialect for the Daba standard; Glottolog lists Nive and Pologozom as dialects of nucl1683. It explicitly distinguishes Daba-propre from Daba-Mazagway (maza1304) and Daba-Kola (separate languoid); the tone statement applies to Daba proper/Pologozom.

sources.note: Ch. 2 Phonologie, §2.5 Les tons (pp. 14-16): every syllable carries its own tone; three level tones H/M/L plus a low falling tone on some subject pronouns; tone patterns restricted by word class; tone has little lexical but real grammatical function. No mention of stress / accent d'intensité anywhere in the document (grep for accent/intensité/ton: only tone diacritics).
